The agency is seeking public input to inform its support of research on a compound being studied as a possible treatment for substance use disorders. A notice published today asks researchers, clinicians, patients, and other stakeholders to submit comments on the design of clinical trials, safety monitoring, and the type of evidence that would be needed to evaluate the compound’s effects. The agency emphasized that the compound is not approved for any use and that its safety has not been established. Of particular interest are questions about cardiac risk, dosing, and the role of psychological support during treatment. Comments will be accepted for 90 days through the federal docket. The agency noted that it would consider the input in developing guidance, and that a public workshop may be scheduled later.
